role.good.goose.info: Just a regular Goose. Survive and finish tasks, or vote out the impostors to win. This role has one vote and cannot be sniped by the Assassin.
role.good.canadian.info:
Your body will automatically be reported by the killer when you are killed or swallowed. These cases will NOT auto-report:
Killed by the Professional, killed by the Sheriff, blown up by a bomb, terrain/environment kills, voted out, or sniped by the Assassin during a meeting.
Entering Pelican Time / Falcon Time / Crow Time after death, dying during those times, fulfilling a team's win condition after death, or if the killer who killed the Canadian Goose dies within the auto-report delay / another body is reported within the delay.
This role has one vote.
role.good.sheriff.info:
You can kill any player, but killing a Goose by mistake is fatal.
Details: You can kill any player, but if you kill a Goose-team player, you die too. Unlimited kills but with a cooldown. Killing a Canadian Goose does not auto-report — you die together instead.
This role has one vote.
role.good.mimic.info:
Ducks see you as one of their own.
Details: You appear in the Duck teammates display.
This role has one vote.
role.good.vigilante.info:
Once per game you can kill one bird — use it wisely.
Details: You may kill one player per game. Even if you kill a Goose, you do not die.
This role has one vote.
role.good.medium.info:
You can sense how many ghosts there are.
Details: You know how many ghosts are currently in the game.
This role has one vote.
role.good.detective.info:
You can investigate players to see if they have killed this round.
Details: Investigate other players to check whether they have killed this round (except Pelican and Demolitionist). This does not reveal their team. Each player can only be checked once per round, so kills after the check won't show.
This role has one vote.
role.good.mortician.info:
You can examine bodies and see their roles.
Details: Use your ability on a body; after 3 seconds the check completes, and you can see their true role during the meeting. Cannot be used on: bomb victims or environment kills that leave no body (e.g. falling off the map).
This role has one vote.
role.good.celebrity.info:
All Geese get an alert when you are killed.
Details: All Goose-team players are alerted when the Celebrity is killed. No alert for: environment deaths, being sniped by the Assassin during voting, or being voted out.
This role has one vote.
role.good.avenger.info:
If you witness a kill, you gain the ability to kill for the host-configured duration.
Details: After witnessing a murder, you briefly gain one kill. The Avenger kill also has a cooldown.
Cases that trigger the ability: a player being directly killed by any means, or the Sheriff dying with a Goose-team player on a miskill.
Cases that do NOT trigger: bomb deaths, environment kills, or if the Avenger loses line of sight (beyond 30 blocks, or while blinded).
This role has one vote.
role.evil.cannibal.info:
Once per game, you can eat a body.
Details: Eat one body per game. Has kill and sabotage abilities.
This role has one vote.
role.evil.morphling.info:
You can morph into other players.
Details: Use your ability on a player to take their appearance. The morph can be saved and lasts 20 seconds. Has kill and sabotage abilities.
This role has one vote.
role.evil.professional.info:
[Full Blood DLC exclusive] Geese cannot see players you kill. When a Goose approaches the body, it auto-reports. The Professional cannot report bodies themselves.
Details: Entity invisibility hides bodies killed by the Professional from the Goose team (other teams can still see them). Goose-team players auto-report when near the body. The Professional cannot report bodies, so killing a Canadian Goose does not auto-report. Has kill and sabotage abilities.
This role has one vote.
role.evil.spy.info:
If you are the only one who votes for a player, after returning to the game you can see that player's role.
Details: During a meeting, if only the Spy votes for a player, you see their true identity at the start of the next meeting. Has kill and sabotage abilities.
This role has one vote.
role.evil.assassin.info:
Twice per game during a meeting, you may guess a player's role. Correct = they die; wrong = you die.
Details: During meetings you can guess a player's identity. Guess right and they die; guess wrong and you die. Only two uses per game. Has kill and sabotage abilities.
This role has one vote.
role.evil.demolitionist.info:
You can plant bombs on other players.
Details: Plant bombs on other players. No kill ability, but can sabotage. Remains from bomb deaths cannot be reported into a meeting, but can be eaten.
After planting, the bomb waits a random delay (default 6-12 seconds) before appearing on the target and starting its countdown. Countdown length is configurable (default 15 seconds). If a meeting starts before the bomb appears, the remaining delay continues after the meeting. If a meeting starts after it appears, the bomb stays active; if less time remains than the floor (default 10 seconds), it is restored to that floor, otherwise the remaining time is kept.
Bombs can be passed between players, but a player who just received one must wait 3 seconds before passing it on. If a bomb carrier is swallowed by the Pelican, the Pelican dies when the countdown ends.
This role has one vote.
role.evil.identitythief.info:
Until a meeting is called, you morph into your most recent kill.
Details: Morph into the player you most recently killed. Lasts indefinitely until your next kill or a meeting starts. Has kill and sabotage abilities.
This role has one vote.
role.evil.ninja.info:
You can kill two birds in range at once, but your kill cooldown is triple.
Details: Kill two players in range at once, but kill cooldown is three times a normal Duck's. Collecting gold ingots can reduce the time.
After cooldown ends, meetings do not reset it. After a meeting ends you only have a 5-second cooldown until your next kill. Has kill and sabotage abilities.
In PoolCore Advance tunnels, kill cooldown decreases by 2 seconds per second.
This role has one vote.
role.evil.invisibility.info:
You can turn invisible.
Details: Go invisible for 10 seconds with a speed boost, but you are blinded while invisible. Has kill and sabotage abilities.
This role has one vote.
role.neutral.dodo.info:
You only win by being voted out.
Details: Win only by being voted out. No active abilities.
This role has one vote.
role.neutral.duelingdodos.info:
Win by killing the other Dueling Dodo, then being voted out.
Details: There are two Dueling Dodos. You only win if the other is dead and you are then voted out. Completing the set number of tasks grants the kill ability and a radar.
This role has one vote.
role.neutral.vulture.info:
Win by eating bodies.
Details: Bodies needed = total living players ÷ 3, rounded down. (6–8 players: 2 bodies; 9–11: 3; 12–14: 4; 15–16: 5). When a body appears, the Vulture's radar keeps pointing to it. Eating has a cooldown.
Bodies from knife kills or bomb remains can both be eaten, with exceptions such as environment kills.
This role has one vote. Does not appear with the Pelican.
role.neutral.pigeon.info:
Infect every living player before another faction wins.
Details: Win by infecting all living players. The host can configure Single Target or AOE infection and its range. Using the ability with no valid target still starts its cooldown. Infection cleanup can occur at meeting start, after meeting end, or never because of meetings; death, leaving, and match cleanup still remove the relevant infection.
Pigeon win has the highest priority. Examples: during a meeting, if the Assassin snipes the only uninfected player, Pigeon wins. During Pelican Time, if the Pelican eats the only uninfected player, Pigeon wins. During Falcon Time, if the Falcon kills the only uninfected player, Pigeon wins.
This role has one vote.
role.neutral.falcon.info:
Survive to the end to win. While you live, Geese can only win by finishing tasks, and Ducks can only win by sabotaging.
Details: Win as the last survivor. Has a kill ability. While the Falcon is alive, Goose-team players can only win via tasks, and Duck-team players can only win via sabotage.
When only 3 living players remain including the Falcon, a 1-minute countdown starts — Falcon Time. Bodies and the emergency bell cannot start meetings.
During Falcon Time: Goose goal becomes [finish tasks, and kill the Falcon if possible]; Duck goal becomes [kill the Falcon]; Falcon goal becomes [survive or kill the others]; other neutrals stay the same. When the timer ends, if the Falcon still lives they win; if the Falcon is dead, settle as normal.
This role has no vote and auto-skips voting. Does not appear with the Pelican.
role.neutral.pelican.info:
Win as the last survivor. You can swallow players whole; they do not die until a meeting is called.
Details: Win as the last survivor by swallowing players whole; they only die when a meeting is called. The more players swallowed in the same round, the longer the cooldown.
Players inside the Pelican can talk. If the Pelican dies before a meeting, all swallowed players are released; but if the Pelican dies to an environment kill, everyone inside dies too. Eating the Celebrity does not alert Goose-team players.
If the Pelican eats a bomb carrier, the Pelican dies when the countdown ends; other players inside are fine. While the Pelican lives, Geese can only win via tasks and Ducks only via sabotage.
When only 3 living players remain including the Pelican, a 1-minute countdown starts — Pelican Time. Bodies and the emergency bell cannot start meetings.
During Pelican Time: Goose goal becomes [finish tasks, and kill the Pelican if possible]; Duck goal becomes [kill the Pelican]; Pelican goal becomes [survive or swallow everyone]; other neutrals stay the same. When the timer ends, if the Pelican still lives they win; if the Pelican is dead, settle as normal.
This player has no vote and auto-skips voting. Does not appear with Falcon or Vulture.

Game settings have been moved to the inventory
version.more.1.info:
1. Fixed many known bugs that could affect gameplay, such as:
Pelican and Falcon timing causing game-end freezes, inventory replacement and menu-level conflicts, some roles' abilities not working, game decision logic, and more
version.more.2.info:
1. Added Goose Duck Index
2. Added game ratings
3. Added high-player ratings
version.more.3.info:
1. Updated the task system—now uses a task pool
2. Added game logs and partial spectator info display
3. Added various new tasks to the Antique map
version.more.4.info:
1. Added a new game map
2. Updated the meeting system for more modern player controls
3. Adjusted end-of-game info display
4. Fixed factions not showing when the game ends
version.more.5.info:
1. Rewrote the outfit-swap logic, improving game performance by at least 3%%
2. Fixed known bugs introduced by the outfit-swap rewrite
version.more.6.info:
1. Rewrote Goose Goose Duck kill logic
2. Added "Updates & Plans"
version.more.7.info: 1. Rewrote the in-game role info menu for Goose Goose Duck
version.more.8.info:
1. The first player to enter a given save is now assigned as Admin
2. Admins can now force-start the game

ggd.role.specialskill.role.canadian: When you are killed or eaten by a Pelican, the killer automatically reports after the configured delay, except for Professionals and Sheriffs

ggd.role.specialskill.role.medium: You can instantly check how many dead players (ghosts) are currently on the map this round. Players swallowed by a Pelican do not count until they are digested.
ggd.role.specialskill.role.detective: You can check whether a player has killed anyone this round up to the moment of your check, except Demolitionists and Pelicans (their kills are indirect)
ggd.role.specialskill.role.mortician: You can check a corpse's role from life. You can check corpses being dragged by an Undertaker [Unimplemented], but not corpses killed by a Demolitionist or Professional
ggd.role.specialskill.role.celebrity: When you die (except to map mechanics or being eaten by a Pelican), all Goose team players receive a message and a sound cue
ggd.role.specialskill.role.avenger: If you witness another player kill someone, you can kill any player for the host-configured duration. This ability can trigger multiple times in a single round
ggd.role.specialskill.role.cannibal: Once per game, you can eat a corpse
ggd.role.specialskill.role.morphling: You can siphon another player's DNA. Unused DNA does not expire. After using it, your appearance becomes the target's for 20 seconds
ggd.role.specialskill.role.professional: Killing a player leaves no information. When a Goose team player approaches a corpse you killed, it auto-reports, but you cannot report corpses yourself
ggd.role.specialskill.role.spy: If you are the only one who voted for a player, you can see their role when the next meeting starts
ggd.role.specialskill.role.assassin: Up to twice per game, once per meeting: snipe a non-Duck player by guessing their correct role in a meeting. You cannot snipe Gravy or Goose. Killing a Lover causes both Lovers to die together
ggd.role.specialskill.role.demolitionist: You kill by planting bombs on other players. Each player can only pass the bomb once, but beware—the bomb can be passed back to you
ggd.role.specialskill.role.identitythief: When you kill another player, you instantly shapeshift into your most recent victim until a meeting is called
ggd.role.specialskill.role.ninja: You can kill two nearby players at once, but your CD is 3x normal. In PoolCore Advance tunnels, kill cooldown decreases by 2 seconds per second.
ggd.role.specialskill.role.invisibility: You can go invisible for a short time. You move faster but can't see anything—and you're not invincible in this state
ggd.role.specialskill.role.vulture: You can eat corpses killed by a Demolitionist. You can eat corpses being dragged by an Undertaker [Unimplemented]. When a corpse appears, you get a radar pointing to it
ggd.role.specialskill.role.pigeon: You can infect other players and win after infecting everyone alive. The host configures when meetings clear infection progress.
ggd.role.specialskill.role.falcon: When only three players remain including you, Falcon Time begins (see Gameplay for details)
ggd.role.specialskill.role.pelican: You kill by swallowing players. Swallowed players truly die when a meeting starts; if you die before then, they are freed. Swallowing a Canadian Goose auto-reports

text.tutorial.stage1.welcome: Welcome to the Goose Goose Duck tutorial! I'll guide you through every stage. Let's start with tasks~
text.tutorial.stage1.task_introduce:
Tasks are a huge help for the Goose (good) team in Goose Goose Duck.
If all Goose-team players fill the task bar above, the Goose team wins instantly — so let me teach you how to finish your first task!
text.tutorial.stage1.tip1: Open your inventory, click the task book, then view and navigate to your current task.
text.tutorial.stage1.tip.start_task: Looks like you found the task trigger! Check slot 2 on your hotbar — the map should be replaced by the task trigger item. Right-click it to start the task~
text.tutorial.stage1.boat_left: You got off the boat early! Return to the task point and accept it again.
text.tutorial.stage1.task.finish_prompt: Nice work — you finished a task that fast.
text.tutorial.stage1.introduce.taskbar:
See the task progress go up? Keep doing tasks until the bar is full and we win!
Also, in real games the host can change how much task progress players need in settings.
text.tutorial.stage1.found.other.player: Huh? Looks like there's another player up ahead — go check it out.
text.tutorial.stage1.finish: Act 1 complete! Whitewater Rush task succeeded.
item.tutorial.task.trigger.lore: Right-click to start the Whitewater Rush task tutorial
text.tutorial.stage1.boat_prompt: Aha! This one's easy — just keep the boat going straight to the end~
text.tutorial.stage1.boat_left_prompt: Oops, forgot to mention — you have to stay on the boat for this task. No worries, just get near where you accepted it to restart.
text.tutorial.stage2.alloy1: [Alloy] Hey, you're good, right? I just walked past your area and saw no entities — only you doing tasks
text.tutorial.stage2.me1: [Me] Yeah, solid good. I'm a big white goose
text.tutorial.stage2.alloy2: [Alloy] Cool, I'm Canadian Goose. Gonna solo for a bit
text.tutorial.stage2.elf1: She said she's Canadian Goose — that's her role. If you don't know it, open your inventory; I've unlocked role info for you.
text.tutorial.stage2.elf2: To avoid confusion, I only unlocked your role and hers. In real games you can view info for every role~
text.tutorial.stage2.elf3: Alright — while nobody's around, let me teach you how to use the Report item in hotbar slot 1~
text.tutorial.stage2.elf4: I've spawned a temporary body in the middle of the pool next door. Go take a look (╹ڡ╹ )
text.tutorial.stage2.elf5: Great, you're near the body — your Report ability is available now. Right-click to report!
text.tutorial.stage2.elf6: Nice! Normally that would call everyone into a meeting. But (╹ڡ╹ ), this body is just for practice, so I stopped the system from starting a meeting. Head back and keep going forward~
text.tutorial.stage2.kuile1: [Kuile] I found Alloy's body on a pillar in the deep pool, and I ran into Ammy on the way, so I think Ammy did it
text.tutorial.stage2.ammy1: [Ammy] You're slandering me! Yeah I bumped into you, but I didn't see anyone on the way — how could I have killed them? I think you self-killed, self-reported, and are trying to frame me!
text.tutorial.stage2.kuile2: [Kuile] As host, I'm locking votes on Ammy
text.tutorial.stage2.ammy2: [Ammy] Who believes you? I'm voting you
text.tutorial.stage2.elf7: (⊙﹏⊙) Uh, this is a bit messy — but one of them is definitely Duck (evil). I remember Alloy said she was Canadian Goose. Try using that clue to figure out who's the bad guy.
text.tutorial.stage2.elf8: When you're ready, open your inventory and pick who to vote for. You've only got 1 minute, or you'll auto-skip!
text.tutorial.stage2.skip_error: You can't skip in this scenario
text.tutorial.stage2.timeout: Looks like you haven't decided yet — let's rewind time~
text.tutorial.stage2.fail_title: Unfortunately, you haven't learned how to use role clues to find the evil player yet
text.tutorial.stage2.success_title: Nice! You found the real bad guy and voted them out
text.tutorial.stage2.success_subtitle1: You've learned how to report and how to reason about roles
text.tutorial.stage2.success_subtitle2: Congrats on finishing the Goose team tutorial — next up, the Duck journey~
text.tutorial.stage3.elf1: Alright — time to learn how to vent!
text.tutorial.stage3.elf2: Venting is exclusive to the Duck team and some special roles
text.tutorial.stage3.elf3: It lets Duck players pop up in front of others without being noticed to kill them, or make a quick escape
text.tutorial.stage3.elf4: Not every map has vents, and they aren't all the same — it depends on the map
text.tutorial.stage3.elf5: Take this map: see the four iron doors at the bottom of the pool ahead? Those are this map's vents
text.tutorial.stage3.elf7: Okay, you're right above a vent — the Enter Vent item in the second-to-last hotbar slot should be active. Right-click to go in~
text.tutorial.stage3.elf8: Also, before you vent, check that no players from other teams are nearby, or your role may get exposed
text.tutorial.stage3.elf9: Nice, you're in the vent. Keep walking forward to the exit
text.tutorial.stage3.elf10: Great — you've learned how to enter and exit vents. Real-game vent networks are way more tangled than this map's. Don't get lost~
text.tutorial.stage3.sewer_wait: Waiting for later-stage players to finish......

text.tutorial.stage4.elf1: Next, let's do Duck-team sabotage tasks! Same as before — open your inventory and click the task book to locate a sabotage
text.tutorial.stage4.elf2: Awesome — we've got two big tools now. One seals the connected pathways of the current room so no one can enter or leave for a bit. The other triggers an emergency task for all players — if they don't finish it before the timer ends, Duck team wins automatically

text.tutorial.stage5.elf3: Use the door-seal tool to cut us off from outside for a bit — then we can strike

role.good.gravy.subtitle: Complete tasks for bounty and stay close to other Geese for protection
role.good.gravy.info: Each completed task adds 100 Goose Coins to your bounty. After your first task, Ducks can see a bounty marker above you. If another living Goose is within the configured protection range, a non-Goose killing ability kills a random nearby Goose instead. Goose killing abilities can kill you directly. Pelican swallowing, voting, environmental deaths, and linked deaths are not killing abilities for this protection. Survive until game end to receive the bounty; if a player kills you, the killer receives it. Assassins cannot snipe you.

role.good.bodyguard.subtitle: Stay near the shared target and intercept ordinary knife attacks
role.good.bodyguard.info: You always appear together with the Hitman. At game start, both of you receive the same target, who cannot be either of you. A compass continuously points to the target and shows the distance. While the target is within protection range, you take ordinary knife attacks for them; whether Goose attacks are intercepted is configurable. If the target is alive when the game ends, you receive 500 Goose Coins. Being swallowed by a Pelican is temporary; a target released after the Pelican dies still counts as alive.
role.evil.hitman.subtitle: Track and personally kill the shared target for a bounty
role.evil.hitman.info: You always appear together with the Bodyguard. At game start, both of you receive the same target, who cannot be either of you. A compass continuously points to the target and shows the distance. Apart from receiving 500 Goose Coins after the game when you personally kill the target, you behave like a normal Duck and can use Duck Potential on PoolCore.

role.neutral.phoenix.info: After the first eligible player or ability death, including a lover's chain death, begin a rebirth countdown. Environmental deaths and banishment cannot trigger rebirth. role.evil.mime.info: You have a normal kill but no Duck Potential. Mark any player, then use Control after its preparation cooldown to leave a dummy that mirrors your movement and view while you control the target's movement and camera.
